title: Shared definitions
description: Building blocks shared by the overlay, module overlay, pluggable, rack and pack schemas.

format.description: The library format this file is written for. Optional; the tools write it, and a later format will change the value.

why.description: Why Danbyte adds or changes this: required on every addition and removal, so a reviewer sees it was deliberate and can offer it upstream to NetBox. Name the source (install guide, data sheet, the hardware itself).
examples: StackPower receptacle on the rear panel (Cisco C9300 HIG); upstream has no StackPower ports

name.description: A component name, exactly as in the NetBox YAML (`{module}` placeholders included).

partNumber.description: A vendor part number, exactly as the vendor prints it.

assetPath.description: A file under `danbyte/`, relative to it (normally `assets/<Vendor>/<file>`). No `..`, no absolute paths.

glbPath.description: A binary glTF 2.0 file (`.glb`) under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.glb`. Stored with Git LFS.

imagePath.description: A WebP or PNG image under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.<face>.webp`. Stored with Git LFS.

ledBinding.description: What lights one LED. `source` is where its state comes from; `modules.status` takes the worst status of the modules in matching bays (`bays:`, or inline as `"modules.status: PS-*"`); `only` lights it only in those colours (a failure LED: `[red]`).

source.description: device.status, device.locate, module.status, modules.status, interface.oper_status, or none (a decorative LED that stays off).

bays.description: modules.status only: the bay names or globs it reads.

only.description: Light the LED only in these colours.

model3d.description: The 3D model of a device or module type (export spec §1-§8). Danbyte assembles a device from its chassis file plus one file per installed module, placed at the chassis' `bay:` empties, and lights `led:` meshes from live status.

file.description: The full-detail model. Budgets: chassis ≤ 150,000 triangles, module ≤ 30,000; ≤ 8 MB.

far.description: The far-distance copy: same origin, outer size and `bay:` / `empty:` / `led:` names. Budgets: chassis ≤ 15,000 triangles, module ≤ 3,000; ≤ 1 MB.

empty.description: What an empty bay shows: the model's `empty:` filler plate, a dark hole, or nothing.

fit.description: `auto` fits the model to the type's size; `native` keeps the model's own size.

up.description: The model's up axis, when not glTF's Y.

front.description: The axis the model's front faces, when not +Z.

leds.description: LED id → binding. Keys are the `led:` mesh names without `led:`; `port:*` covers every `led:port:` LED. An LED without an entry stays off.

renders.description: Device types: face photos rendered in Blender from the model (export spec §12). Danbyte stores them as the type's photos and places its ports on them.

model_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the `file` glb the photos were rendered from; `validate` checks it matches.

modules.description: Bay name → module part number installed in the render.

rackMount.description: How the device sits on a rack's rails (export spec §3, §8 "Rack mounting"). Danbyte puts the ear plane on the rack's front rail and the faceplate at the chosen position's offset.

ears.description: false: no rack ears (shelf, sliding rails, free-standing). Default true.

positions.description: Ear positions the install guide offers: faceplate in front of the ear plane, in mm (+ toward the rack front; a recessed front fitting is negative).

default.description: The fitting the box ships with.

rails.description: The rail kit it is meant for.

after.description: Insert right after this existing component (default: at the end of the list).

before.description: Insert right before this existing component.

remove.description: Components to drop from the upstream list, each with why. Use sparingly; a wrong upstream entry is better fixed upstream.

type.description: A NetBox interface type slug (for example `1000base-t`, `cisco-stackwise-480`).

stack.description: Danbyte: this data port carries the stack link (VSF, IRF, iStack…). Only where the vendor's stacking guide names it; ports typed with a stacking type are stack ports already.

type.description: A NetBox power port type, or a Danbyte extension type (`cisco-stackpower`).

modules.description: Danbyte: module types that fit this bay, by part number, from the data sheet (every supported part, not only those in a pack). Danbyte offers them first when someone installs a module. NetBox ignores the key.

interfacePatch.description: Fields to change on an interface that upstream already has, found by its name. Only the fields given change; `why` is optional on a change.

interfaceAdd.description: An interface upstream lacks, in NetBox's own fields plus `why`. Added at the end of the list unless `after` / `before` say where.

interfaceSection.description: `interfaces:` patched by name. Each key is the name of an interface upstream has, mapped to the fields to change; `add:` lists new ones (each with `why`), `remove:` drops upstream ones (each with `why`). The upstream list itself is never rewritten.

extensionTypes.description: Port types Danbyte reads that NetBox doesn't list yet, by component class. A merged record may use them although NetBox's own schema would refuse them; `validate` accepts exactly these. Offer them upstream when NetBox would take them.

power-port.description: `cisco-stackpower`: a Cisco StackPower receptacle (Catalyst 9300 / 9300X). It carries power between stack members, so it is a power port, not an interface.
